item.title: Exploring Observability with OpenTelemetry and Jaeger
item.description: I have a Telegram echo-bot written in Go, running locally on my laptop. As a DevOps/SRE enthusiast, I wanted to enhance it with logging and observability. After seeing OpenTelemetry mentioned in several job postings, I decided to configure it to add observability to my project. OpenTelemetry offers two main options for instrumentation: Zero-code instrumentation: Automatic and minimal setup. Code-based instrumentation: Requires modifications to the codebase. I chose the first option for its simplicity and ease of use.

item.title: Vim
item.description: Surviving Vim: A Beginner’s Short Guide Switching from Notepad++ on Windows to Linux terminal text editors can be quite a shift. Nano is simple and user-friendly with its prompts, but Vim can be daunting at first. I remember when I first opened Vim, I struggled so much with its commands that I ended up closing the terminal because I couldn’t figure out how to quit. After some frustration, I watched explanations by Sander van Vugt to get a better grasp of Vim.
